title: II.13: Fugue in F# major

groocock.chapter: 7 Group 2: Fugues for Three Voices, without Stretto

entries.notes: real answer; starts at once in the dominant
decorated with a written-out turn instead of a trill
with two-bar extension (recalls falling sequence of episodes)
written-out turn instead of trill; CS altered in bar 79

episodes.material: rising scale steps of bars 1-2 by augmentation with other subject figures, direct and inverted, in three-part interchangeable counterpoint (bars 13,15,17,19 cyclic interchange)
episodes.sequence: rising scale of an octave and a fifth across registers

episodes.material: end of subject entry repeated, middle voice adds thirds, then soprano sixths; first half repeated a tone higher; running bass formed from rising steps of ep.1 (harmonic minor steps)
complex interchange of episode 1 (cyclic order in the opposite direction); virtually same bass as ep.1 with upper voices interchanged
repeat of episode 2 with almost the same bass and upper voices interchanged

countersubjects.first: bar 4 (joined to subject by octave leap)
countersubjects.interchange: fifteenth (octave possible only up to first note of bar 7)
countersubjects.notes: joined to subject by octave leap (bar 4) or seventh (8, 20); given a different ending on four occasions (35, 55, 67, 79); middle voice continuation at bar 8 could have been a second CS (returns 33-36 soprano, 65-68 middle) but never used as bass. Listed among fifteenth interchange p.13; CS unaltered with subject entry p.15

subject.notes: unique in the 48 in starting on the leading-note; real answer chosen because a tonal answer would spoil the sequential shape (p.6); every entry exactly like the opening except bars 20 and 76 (turn written out)

key_plan: Group 2 table: Exp I V I | Counterexp EP I EP V I | Dev vi EP IV | Final EP I V I

claims.claim: Gavotte rhythm in four-bar phrases throughout, except two places in the final section.
Simple exposition, each voice entering without delay.
Episode 1 uses three-part interchangeable counterpoint in cyclic order (bars 13, 15, 17, 19).
Episode 3 is a complex interchange of episode 1, cyclic order reversed.
Real answer used because a tonal answer would spoil the sequential pattern of the subject.
